messages.mes:
*Cool wind moves through the rough grass around Alaric Red's boots.*

*The last thing that belongs to Earth is still there in memory—an old life, a world without visible mana, Classes, or this impossible second beginning. The present is different: the smell of soil and distant woodsmoke, an unfamiliar sky, and stone walls beyond the public road.*

*Alaric Red is already standing on an uncultivated roadside verge outside the nearby city. Cultivated fields and fenced holdings begin farther away. No one is close enough to have witnessed the instant of arrival.*

*The body is Human, healthy, and eighteen years old. Simple traveler's clothes are already being worn; a small pouch holding five silver rests at the belt. The memories are still from Earth.*

*A translucent interface opens across Alaric Red's vision.*

`SYSTEM INITIALIZATION COMPLETE`
`Origin: Earth`
`World: Avereth`
`Race: Human`
`Age: 18`
`Level: 1 | Rank: F`

`BASE STATS`
`STR 5 | VIT 5 | AGI 5 | INT 5 | PER 5 | WIL 5`

`Location: Public roadside verge outside Alderwatch, Valedorn Crown`
`Arrival Witnesses: NONE`
`Starting Possessions: Simple Traveler's Clothes | Small Pouch | 5 Silver`
`Local Common Language: Integrated`
`Mandatory Quest: NONE`

`CHARACTER CREATION — STEP 1/2`
`Choose your Base Class:`

`Warrior   — Favored Stats: STR / VIT`
`Mage      — Favored Stats: INT / WIL`
`Guardian  — Favored Stats: VIT / WIL`
`Duelist   — Favored Stats: STR / AGI`
`Ranger    — Favored Stats: AGI / PER`

`Your chosen Class immediately applies +1 to both Favored Stats at Level 1.`
`After choosing a Class, select exactly 2 Skills from that Class's Base Skill Pool.`

`Reply with your Class choice.`

*The System waits. Story time does not move during Character Creation.*

messages.mes:
The road took him down from the verge between plowed fields, and Alderwatch grew as he walked: first the walls, grey stone patched with darker mortar, then the sound of the city itself, cart wheels and a hammer somewhere and a dog barking itself hoarse. The gate stood open. A guard in a quilted jerkin glanced at the staff slung across his back, saw nothing worth a question, and waved him through with the rest of the morning traffic.

Inside, the street smelled of bread and horse dung. A woman argued over the price of geese. Two boys chased a hoop past his knees. Alderwatch did not care that he had arrived from nowhere; the city had its own morning to get on with.

He asked once, of a carter unloading casks, and the man tipped his chin up the hill without stopping work. "Guild? Left at the well, follow the blue shutters."

The Guild hall was easy to find after that: a broad stone building with those blue shutters folded back, a wooden sign carved with a crossed sword and arrow above the door, and a steady coming and going of armed people. A woman in mail ducked out through the door, adjusting a sword belt. Somewhere inside, a crowd of voices and the clink of coin.

The door was heavy oak, worn smooth at the handle. It opened at a pull onto a hall that smelled of tallow and old leather — long notice boards papered with contract slips, a line of tables before a counter, bench seating along the walls. A few adventurers looked up when the door moved, then went back to their cups and their arguments. Behind the counter, a clerk with ink-stained fingers was already watching him, waiting to see if he wanted anything.

messages.mes:
"Red," the clerk repeated, already pulling a ledger across the counter. "Fresh face, so I'll say the whole thing once."

She flipped the ledger open and dipped a pen. "Registration is two silver, one time, and it buys you a standing in the rolls and the right to take contracts off that board there." A nod toward the papered notice boards. "You start at Novice. That's your Guild standing, not how strong you are — that's a separate thing, your Power Rank, and the measuring stone tells us that, not me. Novice work is what it sounds like. Escorts, deliveries, culling rats out of cellars. It gets better from there."

The pen hovered. "Two silver, and I write your name in. Do you want it?"

messages.mes:
The coins crossed the counter, two silver into the clerk's hand, and she wrote the name in a careful hand: *Alaric Red*. The ledger line got a flourish of her pen and a dab of sand to dry the ink.

"Right. This way, and don't touch anything."

She reached beneath the counter and hauled up a faceted crystal the size of a fist, set in a tarnished brass stand, and put it in front of him. "Hand on the stone. It reads what you are, not what you say you are."

The crystal was cool under his palm. A flicker of light turned inside it, pale and unhurried, and settled.

"F," she said, reading the facet. "Lowest band, everyone starts somewhere. That's your Power Rank, nothing to be ashamed of — it moves when you do." She pulled a flat wooden case from under the counter, opened it, and slid a small iron plate across the counter to him. It was the size of a coin but thinner, stamped with the Guild's crossed sword and arrow, and it warmed faintly at his touch. "Your plate. It knows who you are, so don't lose it — replacing one costs more than registering did. Show it at any branch and the rolls will vouch for you. Contracts, payouts, all of it goes through that."

She wiped her pen and slid the ledger away. "You're in, Red. Novice rank, board's over there on the left wall. Anything the clerk's desk has to do — taking a contract, turning one in — comes back to me."
